{
      question: "A user forgot their password and needs to access their computer. What steps do you take to help them?",
      answer: "**Step 1: Identity Verification**
• Ask security questions or check employee ID
• Verify caller through established protocols
• Confirm authorization for password reset

**Step 2: Password Reset Process**
• Access Active Directory or identity management portal
• Locate and select the user's account
• Generate temporary password (complex, expires on first use)
• Provide password securely (in-person or verified phone)

**Step 3: User Instructions**
• Instruct immediate password change upon login
• Remind of requirements: 8+ characters, uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters
• Explain password best practices

**Step 4: Documentation**
• Record in ticket system: date, time, verification method
• Note any issues or special circumstances
• Update user contact information if needed

**Step 5: Follow-up**
• Show self-service password reset portal
• Provide documentation for future reference
• Confirm successful login after reset"

{
      question: "How do you properly document a support ticket from start to resolution?",
      answer: "**Initial Contact Documentation**
• User name and contact information
• Date/time of request
• Problem description (brief but specific)
• Priority level and business impact

**During Troubleshooting**
• Each step taken with timestamps
• Results of each action (success/failure)
• Error messages captured verbatim
• Time spent on each troubleshooting phase
• Tools and resources used

**Resolution Details**
• Root cause identified
• Solution implemented
• Parts/software/licenses used
• Total resolution time
• Verification steps performed

**Closure Requirements**
• Clear problem/solution summary
• User confirmation of resolution
• Knowledge base articles referenced or created
• Proper categorization for metrics
• Follow-up actions if needed

**Benefits**: Builds knowledge base, tracks patterns, improves future response times"

{
      question: "A new employee needs their workstation set up. Walk through the process.",
      answer: "**Pre-Setup Review**
• Check new hire ticket: username, department, software requirements
• Verify start date and urgency
• Gather necessary licenses and access credentials

**Hardware Preparation**
• Unbox and inspect all components
• Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse
• Verify power and network connections
• Check for any physical damage

**System Configuration**
• Enter BIOS to verify hardware detection
• Boot from network/USB for imaging
• Join domain with proper naming convention
• Apply latest Windows updates and patches

**User Setup**
• Create domain user profile
• Install required software (Office, department-specific apps)
• Configure Outlook with email account
• Set up OneDrive/cloud storage

**Peripheral Configuration**
• Install and test printer drivers
• Map network printers and drives
• Configure scanner/other devices
• Test all USB ports and connections

**Final Validation**
• Test all applications launch correctly
• Verify internet/intranet access
• Confirm security software is active
• Create desktop shortcuts for common resources

**Handover**
• Document setup completion
• Provide quick reference guide
• Share IT contact information
• Schedule follow-up if needed"

{
      question: "Walk through the complete process of fusion splicing two fibers, including preparation and testing.",
      answer: "**Workspace Setup**
• Clean, stable surface away from wind/dust
• Proper lighting for visibility
• Fusion splicer on stable platform
• All tools organized and accessible

**Cable Preparation**
• Measure and mark strip lengths accurately
• Score and remove outer jacket carefully
• Clean buffer tubes with appropriate wipes
• Separate fibers without inducing stress

**Fiber Preparation**
• Strip fiber using precision strippers (1.25 inches typical)
• Clean with 99% isopropyl alcohol
• Use lint-free wipes, one-directional motion
• Inspect fiber end for contamination

**Cleaving Process**
• Use precision cleaver with fresh blade
• Ensure proper strip length in cleaver
• Apply consistent pressure for clean break
• Verify cleave angle (<0.5 degrees)

**Fusion Process**
• Place fibers in V-grooves carefully
• Ensure proper alignment in splicer
• Close wind cover before fusion
• Observe arc fusion on screen

**Quality Checks**
• Inspect splice on splicer screen
• Verify estimated loss (<0.05dB target)
• Look for bubbles or alignment issues
• Re-splice if not acceptable

**Splice Protection**
• Slide heat shrink over splice point
• Place in heater for proper time
• Ensure sleeve fully contracts
• Allow cooling before handling

**Tray Management**
• Route fibers maintaining bend radius
• Secure in designated slots
• Avoid crossing or tangling
• Label per documentation standards

**Final Testing**
• OTDR test bi-directionally
• Verify splice loss within specs
• Check for reflectance issues
• Document all results

**Common Issues**: Contamination, poor cleave angles, incorrect fusion parameters"

{
      question: "Explain how to use an OTDR to locate a fault in a fiber optic cable, including trace interpretation.",
      answer: "**Initial OTDR Setup**
• Select wavelength: 1310nm (general) or 1550nm (long distance)
• Set pulse width: shorter for accuracy, longer for distance
• Configure averaging time for noise reduction
• Set appropriate distance range

**Launch Cable Setup**
• Use minimum 500m launch cable
• Ensure all connections are clean
• Match fiber type to system under test
• Verify launch cable condition

**Test Execution**
• Connect OTDR to launch cable
• Initiate trace acquisition
• Wait for averaging to complete
• Save baseline trace for comparison

**Trace Interpretation**
• **Axes**: Vertical = power (dB), Horizontal = distance
• **Slopes**: Downward = fiber attenuation
• **Events**: Sudden drops = connectors, splices, breaks

**Event Identification**
• **Connectors**: Small loss with reflection
• **Mechanical splices**: Loss with reflection
• **Fusion splices**: Loss without reflection
• **Breaks**: Large loss with high reflection

**Fault Location Process**
• Identify anomalous event on trace
• Note distance reading to event
• Account for cable slack (3-5% typical)
• Consider actual cable routing

**Advanced Analysis**
• Use two-point loss measurement
• Check event reflectance values
• Compare with baseline traces
• Test bi-directionally for accuracy

**Ghost Detection**
• Identify events beyond fiber end
• Recognize as reflections of real events
• Calculate actual location mathematically
• Exclude from analysis

**Macro-bend Detection**
• Appears as gradual loss increase
• May not show reflection
• Common at incorrect cable storage
• Verify with visual inspection

**Documentation**
• Save traces with descriptive names
• Export data for reports
• Maintain historical records
• Create event maps for reference"
